title: Every coordinate face of a finite simultaneous SNC root algebra is regular
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring such that $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, $r\geq0$, be equations of the pairwise distinct reduced irreducible branches of a strict normal crossings boundary on $X$, with these branches precisely the closed subschemes $V(t_i)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $n\geq1$ be an integer whose image $n\cdot1_A$ is a unit, and put $$C_n=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),$$ using multivariate polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then for every subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ the quotient ring $C_n/(x_j)_{j\in J}$ is a regular Noetherian ring: each of its prime localizations is a regular local ring. Equivalently, the closed subscheme $V(x_j:j\in J)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C_n$ is regular. No irreducibility or nonemptiness of the intersections $V(t_j:j\in J)$ is assumed: they may be empty or disconnected, and then the zero ring is allowed. For $J=\varnothing$ this is the regularity of $C_n$ itself; for $r=0$ one has $C_n=A$.

proof.text: Derive a bijective enumeration of the irreducible boundary components from hdistinct and hbranches, using injectivity of image under the support inclusion. Each component is irreducible, so its zero locus has prime radical ideal. The reduced quotient hypothesis identifies this radical with (t_i). The quotient-spectrum range formula therefore supplies precisely the branch hypotheses of [lem-sfb-snc-root-local-presentation]. Apply that lemma to obtain Noetherianity and the regular local coefficient strata with their dimension equalities.

proof.text: Write P=A[x_i] and F=(x_i^n-t_i)+(x_j:j in J). The third isomorphism theorem identifies the given iterated quotient with E=P/F. The relations give x_i^n=t_i, x_j=0 and hence t_j=0 for j in J. Construct inverse ring maps between E and (A/(t_j:j in J))[x_i:i outside J]/(x_i^n-t_i), using evaluation and quotient lifts [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Their composites fix coefficients and each surviving coordinate; killed coordinates vanish. Noetherianity of E follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

proof.text: At a prime q of E, contract to p in A and set R=A_p. Regularity of Spec A identifies R with a regular local stalk [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Membership of t_i/1 in the maximal ideal is equivalent to t_i in p. For each L of such indices the local-presentation conclusion supplies the required regular local quotient and dimension. Since t_j=0 in E, J consists of such indices. The image of n is a unit. Apply [lem-sfb-transverse-local-root-family-regular] with coefficient stratum J and complementary root set to get its partial root algebra regular.

proof.text: Polynomial localization and quotient localization identify (A minus p)^(-1)E with R[x_i]/F_R: the coefficient map sends F to F_R on its displayed generators. The face presentation from step 2 identifies this ring with the regular transverse root algebra of step 3. The denominators avoid q by contraction. Extend q to this localization; it is prime and contracts back to q. Localizing there is E_q by the localization universal property. Transport regular locality along the resulting ring equivalence. Every E_q is regular local and E is Noetherian, so E is regular. The iterated-quotient equivalence proves the statement, including empty and disconnected strata.
